style.vernacular: Nordic capital: ochre, yellow and cream plastered apartment blocks of four to six storeys from the 19th and early 20th century with copper-green or dark sheet roofs; red-brick National Romantic buildings; pale functionalist blocks of the 1930s; Million Programme concrete and render housing suburbs; Falu red timber cottages in the archipelago; medieval fieldstone churches in the countryside; glass-and-metal malls and offices in the suburbs.
style.ornament: Plastered facades in earthy ochres with white window frames and stone-grey plinths, steep copper or sheet roofs with dormers and chimneys, National Romantic brick towers and turrets, Falu red timber with white corner boards, medieval stepped gables and fieldstone, runestones with red-painted serpent bands.

sources.what: National Romantic style in brick and wood (Stockholm City Hall 1903-23), functionalism broke through after the 1930 Stockholm Exhibition, Million Programme suburbs from 1965
Old town: medieval alleys, cobbled streets, North German influence, gabled merchant houses, baroque Royal Palace
medieval fieldstone church with 1776 rebuild; typical Uppland rural church
